cues.en: Presenter: Now I'm going to tell you about the Spearman rank correlation, which is usually just called the Spearman correlation.
cues.zh: 講師：現在介紹史皮爾曼秩相關，通常直接稱為史皮爾曼相關。

cues.en: This is the dominant method for non-parametric correlations as an alternative to the Pearson correlation.
cues.zh: 這是無母數相關的主要方法，可作為皮爾森相關的替代方案。

cues.en: So I'm gonna start this video by showing this slide again of Anscobe's quartet.
cues.zh: 首先再次展示安斯康姆四重奏的投影片。

cues.en: This is exactly the same slide that I showed in the previous video where I identified some of the problems with the Pearson correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: 這與上一支影片的投影片完全相同，當時指出皮爾森相關係數的一些問題。

cues.en: So the conclusion there was that Pearson's are, so the regular correlation coefficient can either inflate or deflate relationships
cues.zh: 結論是，皮爾森 r，也就是一般相關係數，可能高估或低估變數之間

cues.en: between variables if those relationships are non-linear, or if they have contain outliers.
cues.zh: 的關係，如果關係是非線性，或包含離群值。

cues.en: So Pearson's R is sensitive to outliers.
cues.zh: 因此，皮爾森 r 對離群值敏感。

cues.en: It can be highly sensitive to outliers or a little bit sensitive to outliers, depending on where the outlier is, how strong it is, how much leverage it has, and so on.
cues.zh: 可能非常敏感，也可能稍微敏感，取決於離群值的位置、強度、槓桿值等等。

cues.en: So the Pearson's correlation coefficient, Pearson's R is appropriate mainly for normally distributed data that do not contain any outliers.
cues.zh: 所以皮爾森相關係數，也就是皮爾森 r，主要適合沒有離群值的常態分布資料。

cues.en: Again, if there's small outliers, it may not be such a big deal if the data aren't exactly perfectly, theoretically, normally distributed, but they're kind of roughly normally distributed
cues.zh: 如果離群值很小，也不一定是大問題；如果資料不完全符合完美的理論常態分布，但大致呈常態，

cues.en: and it's also fine.
cues.zh: 也沒有關係。

cues.en: So there's some wiggle room here, but Pearson's correlation is really just meant for normal distribution data without any outliers.
cues.zh: 這裡有一些彈性，但皮爾森相關原本就是用於沒有離群值的常態分布資料。

cues.en: Now, when you have a Spearman correlation on normally distributed data that will converge with Pearson. In this case, they are the same up to two numbers.
cues.zh: 對常態分布資料計算史皮爾曼相關，結果會趨近皮爾森相關。這個例子中，兩者到小數點後兩位

cues.en: After the decimal point, they'll start to diverge eventually.
cues.zh: 都相同，之後才開始出現差異。

cues.en: And now to be clear, the Spearman correlation is not some like amazing magic bullet that's always going to provide the best answer.
cues.zh: 說清楚一點，史皮爾曼相關並不是什麼神奇萬靈丹，並不總是提供最佳答案。

cues.en: The main benefit of the Spearman correlation is that it is robust to outliers.
cues.zh: 它的主要優點，是對離群值穩健。

cues.en: So, it's not sensitive to outliers.
cues.zh: 也就是對離群值不敏感。

cues.en: You see that here where the correlation is almost one between these two variables here, despite the presence of this outlier.
cues.zh: 這裡可以看到，雖然有這個離群值，兩個變數之間的相關仍然幾乎為 1。

cues.en: Okay, so how does the Spearman correlation work?
cues.zh: 史皮爾曼相關如何運作？

cues.en: Well, I'm going to just describe it in this slide and then I'll explain the algorithm for it in the next slide.
cues.zh: 先在這張投影片描述，下一張再解釋演算法。

cues.en: So it's often called Spearman's rho, Spearman's correlation.
cues.zh: 它常稱為史皮爾曼 rho，或史皮爾曼相關。

cues.en: It tests for a monotonic relationship.
cues.zh: 它檢驗的是單調關係。

cues.en: And it doesn't actually matter whether the true relationship is linear or non-linear.
cues.zh: 真正關係是線性還是非線性，其實不重要。

cues.en: The only thing that matters for Spearman is that it is a monotonic relationship.
cues.zh: 對史皮爾曼而言，唯一重要的是關係是否單調。

cues.en: So let me define this term just in case you're not familiar with it.
cues.zh: 如果你不熟悉，先定義這個詞。

cues.en: So monotonic refers to increasing or decreasing numbers that has nothing to do with the spacing between those numbers.
cues.zh: 單調指數字持續增加或減少，與數字之間的間距無關。

cues.en: So here we have a series of numbers, and this is a region with monotonic increase.
cues.zh: 這裡有一連串數字，這個區域是單調遞增。

cues.en: Notice that every point is higher than the previous point.
cues.zh: 注意，每個點都高於前一個點。

cues.en: Now some points are much higher, some points are only a little bit higher, but every point is higher than the previous point.
cues.zh: 有些點高很多，有些只高一點，但每個點都比前一個高。

cues.en: So that is a monotonic increase.
cues.zh: 這就是單調遞增。

cues.en: Here we have a monotonic decrease.
cues.zh: 這裡則是單調遞減。

cues.en: Again, every point is lower than the previous point and it doesn't matter for monotonicity whether the previous point is really a, you know,
cues.zh: 同樣，每個點都低於前一個。對單調性而言，不論是

cues.en: whether it's really a lot lower like this, or only a little bit lower like this.
cues.zh: 像這樣低很多，還是像這樣只低一點，都沒有關係。

cues.en: Okay, and then here, we have a situation where we have a non-monotonic relationship across the data.
cues.zh: 這裡則是資料之間有非單調關係的情況。

cues.en: So this data point is higher, then it gets lower and so on.
cues.zh: 這個資料點較高，接著變低，依此類推。

cues.en: So monotonic increase, monotonic decrease, and non-monotonic.
cues.zh: 所以這是單調遞增、單調遞減，以及非單調。

cues.en: So the Spearman correlation is going to be identifying any linear relationships in monotonic transforms of the data.
cues.zh: 史皮爾曼相關會辨識，對資料做單調轉換後的線性關係。

cues.en: So how does it work?
cues.zh: 它如何運作？

cues.en: Well, there's a reason why we call it the Spearman rank correlation.
cues.zh: 我們稱它為史皮爾曼「秩」相關，是有原因的。

cues.en: And the way it works is it's actually pretty straightforward.
cues.zh: 運作方式其實相當直接。

cues.en: All you do is transform both of the variables to rank.
cues.zh: 只要把兩個變數都轉換成秩。

cues.en: And you already know that, this is just a quick reminder.
cues.zh: 這你已經學過，這裡快速提醒。

cues.en: So here we have a bunch of numbers.
cues.zh: 這裡有一組數字。

cues.en: Now the differences between these numbers in terms of their, you know, distances on the real axis are quite significant.
cues.zh: 這些數字在實數軸上的距離差異相當大。

cues.en: You know, these two are pretty close to each other.
cues.zh: 這兩個非常接近。

cues.en: This is kind of far apart, and this is super duper, duper far away, but we convert these to rank and we just end up with their ordinal position.
cues.zh: 這兩個有點遠，而這個非常非常遠。不過轉成秩後，只剩排序位置。

cues.en: So minus 40 gets to be the first zero and one, and then this, whatever this huge number is, ends up being number four.
cues.zh: 負 40 排第一，接著是 0 和 1，而這個不管有多大的數字，最後都排第 4。

cues.en: So we convert both variables that we're going to correlate X and Y into rank.
cues.zh: 將要計算相關的 X 與 Y 都轉換成秩。

cues.en: So from this into this, and then maybe you can already guess where this is going.
cues.zh: 從這樣變成這樣，你可能已經猜到接下來要做什麼。

cues.en: Step two is to compute the regular Pearson correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: 第二步，計算一般的皮爾森相關係數。

cues.en: Except we're not computing the correlation on the original data.
cues.zh: 但不是對原始資料計算相關。

cues.en: We are computing the correlation on the ranks.
cues.zh: 而是對秩計算相關。

cues.en: And that is why the Spearman correlation is robust to outliers.
cues.zh: 這就是史皮爾曼相關對離群值穩健的原因。

cues.en: It's robust to scaling effects and why it is just looking for monotonic relationships 'cause we've transformed this into a monotonic scaling
cues.zh: 它對縮放效果穩健，也只尋找單調關係，因為我們把它轉換到單調的尺度，

cues.en: to go one, two, three, four, I guess I should say four, one, three, two.
Okay. So very simple.
cues.zh: 好，非常簡單。

cues.en: That's how you do a Spearman correlation.
cues.zh: 這就是史皮爾曼相關的做法。

cues.en: Convert to rank and then apply the regular Pearson correlation that you already learned about.
cues.zh: 轉換成秩，再套用已經學過的一般皮爾森相關。

cues.en: The P-value is exactly the same as for the regular Pearson coefficient.
cues.zh: P 值的做法與一般皮爾森係數完全相同。

cues.en: So I've just reproduced this here, but this is not a new equation.
cues.zh: 我只是把公式再放一次，這不是新的方程式。

cues.en: I've already introduced you to how you compute statistical significance of a correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: 之前已經介紹如何計算相關係數的統計顯著性。

cues.en: So you can see why the Spearman correlation is robust to outliers, because this is a strong outlier here in this little dataset.
cues.zh: 你可以看到史皮爾曼相關為什麼對離群值穩健，因為在這個小資料集中，這裡有一個很強的離群值。

cues.en: But here, it's no longer an outlier.
cues.zh: 但轉換後，它就不再是離群值。

cues.en: We don't have any outliers when we convert to rank.
cues.zh: 轉成秩之後，就沒有離群值。

cues.en: Now you might remember from the section on normalization and dealing with outliers that I said that in general, there are two strategies for dealing
cues.zh: 你可能記得，在正規化與處理離群值的單元中，我說一般有兩種策略來處理

cues.en: with outliers, depending on your assumptions about where those outliers come from and what they mean.
cues.zh: 離群值，取決於你對它們來源與意義的假設。

cues.en: So the one strategy was to remove outliers from the data, and the second strategy is to include those outliers in the data,
cues.zh: 第一種策略是從資料中移除離群值，第二種則是把離群值留在資料中，

cues.en: but use analysis methods that are robust to those outliers.
cues.zh: 但使用對離群值穩健的分析方法。

cues.en: So this is like, you know, this is such a huge outlier.
cues.zh: 這個離群值實在太大。

cues.en: I obviously, I just made up these numbers here, but if this were real data, then probably this is something you would want to remove from the dataset because this is probably not a valid data point,
cues.zh: 這些數字顯然是我編的，但若是真實資料，你大概會想把它移除，因為它可能不是有效的資料點。

cues.en: but you can imagine that there will be other times when a data point is a little bit unusual.
cues.zh: 但你可以想像，有時某個資料點只是有一點不尋常。

cues.en: It's a little bit outside the distribution of the other data, but it's not necessarily a bad data.
cues.zh: 稍微落在其他資料的分布之外，但不一定是不好的資料。

cues.en: You believe it is real data and you don't want to exclude it, but you also don't want to have a biased or inflated or just inaccurate measure of the correlation.
cues.zh: 你認為它是真實資料，不想排除，但也不想得到有偏差、膨脹，或不準確的相關指標。

cues.en: So that's why you leave it in and you use a Spearman correlation.
cues.zh: 因此，把它留下來，並使用史皮爾曼相關。

cues.en: All right, so in this video, you learned about the main non-parametric method for computing correlations, which is the Spearman rank correlation.
cues.zh: 這支影片學到了計算相關的主要無母數方法，也就是史皮爾曼秩相關。
